cues.en: The rest of this course is focused on something called mechanistic interpretability.
cues.zh: 剩下課程聚焦機制可解釋性。

cues.en: Mechanistic interpretability is a detailed investigation into how information is processed and represented inside AI models.
cues.zh: 詳細研究 AI 內部如何處理、表徵資訊。

cues.en: It's all fairly technical, and there will be a lot of coding and a respectable amount of math.
cues.zh: 相當技術性，有很多程式與一定程度數學。

cues.en: But before getting to any of the details in this section of the course, I want to introduce you to
cues.zh: 但深入前，先介紹

cues.en: the concepts, the relevance and the general criticisms of mechanistic interpretability, which is often shortened to mech interp.
cues.zh: 概念、重要性、一般批評；常簡稱 mech interp。

cues.en: The big picture overall 30,000 foot view of mechanistic interpretability is that its overarching goal
cues.zh: 從三萬英尺的宏觀來看，總目標

cues.en: is to understand how knowledge and concepts are represented inside Llms, and how the operations are implemented.
cues.zh: 是理解 LLM 如何表徵知識、概念，如何實作運算。

cues.en: It is often described as trying to reverse engineer how llms actually work.
cues.zh: 常被稱為逆向工程，弄清實際運作。

cues.en: Or you could think of it like trying to understand how the llms think.
cues.zh: 也可想成理解 LLM 如何思考，

cues.en: Although Llms don't really think in the way that humans do.
cues.zh: 雖然與人類的思考不同。

cues.en: And why do people do mech interp research?
cues.zh: 為何做這種研究？

cues.en: What is the purpose?
cues.zh: 目的？

cues.en: There are several goals, several applications.
cues.zh: 有幾種目標、應用。

cues.en: One of the main ones is trying to improve AI safety.
cues.zh: 一個主要目標，是改善安全，

cues.en: For reasons that I will get into in more detail in the next video.
cues.zh: 下一支會詳談。

cues.en: In addition, a better understanding of how models work internally can also lead to improved fine tuning and instruction tuning.
cues.zh: 了解內部，也有助改善微調、指令微調，

cues.en: Better and more precise quantitative evaluations and also llms are just mysterious complex systems,
cues.zh: 讓量化評估更好、更精確。LLM 也是神祕複雜系統，

cues.en: and there is certainly value and merit in trying to understand how complex systems work, simply because they are there and we humans are curious.
cues.zh: 只因它存在、人類好奇，就值得研究。

cues.en: We want to understand things around us.
cues.zh: 想理解周遭。

cues.en: How do people go about doing mech interp research?
cues.zh: 如何研究？

cues.en: Of course, you will learn a lot of techniques in the rest of this course, but the general idea is
cues.zh: 剩下會學很多技術，但一般概念是

cues.en: to extract and perform machine learning or statistical analyses on the trained weights in the model.
cues.zh: 取出訓練後權重，做機器學習、統計分析。

cues.en: Although mostly, most often we are working with the activations inside the model.
cues.zh: 不過更常處理內部啟用值。

cues.en: And when I say activations, I'm referring to the numerical values of the token embeddings vectors as
cues.zh: 也就是詞元嵌入向量在

cues.en: they pass through the model and get multiplied by all of the weights.
cues.zh: 通過模型、乘權重時的數值。

cues.en: So the activations actually change depending on the tokens and the context.
cues.zh: 會隨詞元與語境變化。

cues.en: And that means that the history of the tokens that the model has already processed in a token sequence affects how a given token is processed.
cues.zh: 所以已處理的詞元歷史，影響目前詞元如何處理。

cues.en: So we can extract all of those activations and we can analyze them and try to relate them to the actual text that the model was processing.
cues.zh: 取出啟用值、分析，再與實際文本連結。

cues.en: And we can also manipulate the activations or the weights in certain parts of the model to see how that causally impacts the behavior of the model.
cues.zh: 也能操弄特定位置的啟用或權重，觀察對行為的因果影響。

cues.en: Well, this is all a little bit high level and abstract.
cues.zh: 這有點高層、抽象。

cues.en: Of course, this will be much more clear starting in the next section, but I want to give you a really simple example just to illustrate the idea.
cues.zh: 下一章會清楚，先用簡例說明。

cues.en: Here we have the equation for a linear regression.
cues.zh: 這是線性迴歸公式。

cues.en: Very simple linear regression.
cues.zh: 很簡單。

cues.en: So imagine we have some output variable y.
cues.zh: 假設輸出變數 y，

cues.en: And we try to predict its value based on these two weights.
cues.zh: 用這兩個權重預測。

cues.en: Beta zero is a bias term and beta one is a weight.
cues.zh: beta_0 是偏置，beta_1 是權重。

cues.en: These are both trainable parameters.
cues.zh: 都是可訓練參數。

cues.en: And then here would be one input value.
cues.zh: 這是一個輸入值。

cues.en: And this epsilon over here is called the residual or unexplained variance.
cues.zh: epsilon 是殘差，或未解釋變異。

cues.en: So to make this more concrete, let's say we are trying to predict your LLM knowledge.
cues.zh: 具體來說，預測你的 LLM 知識。

cues.en: Maybe this is a score on an exam.
cues.zh: 也許是考試分數。

cues.en: And then we say that we can predict your LLM knowledge based on how many hours you spend studying in this course and other online resources.
cues.zh: 依你花在本課與其他網路資源的學習時數，預測知識。

cues.en: Mechanistic interpretability in a simple linear regression would mean interpreting these two trained parameters in the model.
cues.zh: 簡單迴歸的機制可解釋性，就是解讀兩個訓練參數。

cues.en: Well, in this case, that is super duper easy.
cues.zh: 這很容易。

cues.en: The value of beta one is literally predicting how the number of hours you spend relates to your exam score.
cues.zh: beta_1 直接預測學習時數與分數關係。

cues.en: If beta one is positive, it means that the more you study, the better you do.
cues.zh: 正值，就表示讀越多，表現越好。

cues.en: If beta one is small, if it's close to zero, then it means that the more you study well, that has
cues.zh: 若接近零，表示多讀

cues.en: no impact or very little impact on your LLM exam score and beta zero.
cues.zh: 對考試分數幾乎沒影響。beta_0，

cues.en: We can interpret as well.
cues.zh: 也能解讀。

cues.en: This would be the score you would get on your exam if the number of hours you studied is zero.
cues.zh: 就是學習零小時時，預測的考試分數。

cues.en: So that's it.
cues.zh: 就這樣。

cues.en: We just did perfect mechanistic interpretability on a simple linear regression model.
cues.zh: 完美解釋了簡單線性迴歸機制。

cues.en: But the thing is that linear regression is has just a couple of variables and a couple of parameters.
cues.zh: 但它只有少數變數、參數，

cues.en: There's no non-linearities.
cues.zh: 沒有非線性，

cues.en: Everything is linear in this equation.
cues.zh: 全部線性。

cues.en: And yet even just with a regression model, if we had multiple variables with interactions between them,
cues.zh: 即使迴歸，多變數又互相交互作用，

cues.en: for example, let's say we also recorded how much you sleep at night on average leading up to your exam.
cues.zh: 例如也記錄考前平均每晚睡多久，

cues.en: And then we found some interaction between your sleeping patterns and your study hours.
cues.zh: 發現睡眠與讀書時數有交互作用，

cues.en: Now even that is a really simple model.
cues.zh: 還是很簡單，

cues.en: And it's already starting to get fairly complicated to mechanistically interpret those weights values.
cues.zh: 權重的機制解讀卻已開始複雜。

cues.en: And that is just a couple of variables and all linear interactions.
cues.zh: 只是少數變數、線性交互作用，

cues.en: But still.
cues.zh: 就如此。

cues.en: The amazing thing of studying Llms is that, at least for open source models, we can just access literally
cues.zh: 研究 LLM 驚人之處，是至少公開模型，

cues.en: every single weight and every single activation value in the model, wherever we want, whenever we want in Python.
cues.zh: 能在 Python，隨時隨地存取每個權重、每個啟用值。

cues.en: So why is mech interp hard?
cues.zh: 那為什麼難？

cues.en: Shouldn't it be pretty straightforward if we can access all the numbers?
cues.zh: 不是有全部數字，就應該很直接嗎？

cues.en: Well, for one thing, the search space is just absolutely unfathomably huge.
cues.zh: 第一，搜尋空間大得難以想像。

cues.en: There are millions or billions of weights.
cues.zh: 幾百萬、幾十億權重，

cues.en: They are organized in different layers and blocks, and the diversity only increases by orders of magnitude when we start pushing text through a model.
cues.zh: 組成層、區塊；送入文本後，多樣性又增加幾個數量級。

cues.en: Because even the activation values of a particular token are not the same each time you push that same token through the model.
cues.zh: 甚至同一詞元每次送入，啟用也不同，

cues.en: If the words before that token are different.
cues.zh: 只要前面的字不同。

cues.en: Here's an analogy that I like to think about.
cues.zh: 我喜歡這個類比。

cues.en: Imagine that I gave you a gigantic data set, a huge matrix that contained all of the pixel color intensity values from a movie.
cues.zh: 假設給你巨大的矩陣，包含整部電影每個像素的色彩強度。

cues.en: That is a huge amount of data.
cues.zh: 資料非常多。

cues.en: You could run tons of interesting analyses looking at spatial temporal dynamics in those data, but
cues.zh: 能做很多時空動態分析，但

cues.en: the color intensity values that each pixel in a movie do not tell you anything about the plot, the
cues.zh: 每個像素的色彩強度，無法告訴你劇情、

cues.en: character development, the cinematography, or really anything about the movie itself.
cues.zh: 人物發展、攝影，或電影本身的內容。

cues.en: And relatedly, it's not even just about having the numbers, because representations and operations are not localized to single dimensions or single neurons.
cues.zh: 同樣，不只擁有數字，因表徵與運算並非局限於單維或單神經元。

cues.en: Instead, the representations are distributed within and across layers.
cues.zh: 分散在同層、跨層。

cues.en: They are extremely non-linear, and they are all context dependent, meaning that presenting the same
cues.zh: 極度非線性，且依語境；同一個字，

cues.en: word will give a very different pattern of activations inside the model, depending on the tokens that preceded that word.
cues.zh: 依前面的詞元，內部啟用就很不同。

cues.en: You will see plenty of examples of this level of complexity over the rest of the course.
cues.zh: 後面會看到很多複雜例子。

cues.en: Furthermore, mechanistic interpretability is a fairly reductionistic approach, but behaviors in llms
cues.zh: 另外，機制可解釋性相當還原論，但 LLM 行為

cues.en: are clearly emergent, and there are multiple levels of investigating networks, from neurons to circuits to layers to translator circuits.
cues.zh: 顯然是湧現的；有多層次研究，從神經元、迴路、層，到轉換器迴路。

cues.en: And then, of course, we have latent components that reflect weighted combinations of many different circuits.
cues.zh: 還有潛在成分，是多個不同迴路的加權組合。

cues.en: So it's really not clear.
cues.zh: 所以不清楚，

cues.en: Certainly not guaranteed that a reductionistic approach taken by mech Interp is going to necessarily lead to meaningful insights.
cues.zh: 也不保證，還原論方法一定帶來有意義洞見。

cues.en: Just like analyzing the pixels in a movie is not necessarily going to tell you about the love story and how that resolves or who wins in some big action scene in the movie?
cues.zh: 像分析電影像素，未必知道愛情故事結局，或動作場面誰贏。

cues.en: Uh oh yes.
cues.zh: 對。

cues.en: And there's even more reasons why McIntyre is difficult.
cues.zh: 還有更多困難。

cues.en: We don't really have a ground truth against which to verify our analyses and our findings.
cues.zh: 沒有標準答案，驗證分析與發現。

cues.en: And that means that just because we apply some fancy machine learning techniques and we get some results,
cues.zh: 用精巧機器學習、得到結果，

cues.en: it doesn't mean that the conclusions that we can draw from those results really are valid and accurate.
cues.zh: 不代表推論有效、準確。

cues.en: The thing is that we don't already know how llms work internally, so we don't know if we are discovering
cues.zh: 不知道內部怎麼運作，所以不確定找到

cues.en: the right answer or just some quirk of an analysis, or maybe a conclusion that we draw is valid, but it doesn't generalize to other situations or other models.
cues.zh: 正解、分析的某個怪現象，或有效結論卻無法泛化到其他情境、模型。

cues.en: And I think I could summarize almost everything in this slide by saying that modern mechanistic interpretability
cues.zh: 這張幾乎可以總結為：現代大型模型的

cues.en: applied to large models is just a very new field.
cues.zh: 機制可解釋性，是很新的領域。

cues.en: And when I say immature here, I'm not referring to like a bunch of 13 year olds making fart jokes.
cues.zh: 說不成熟，不是指十三歲孩子講放屁笑話。

cues.en: This is more of a scientific term that new disciplines in science tend to be rough, descriptive, full
cues.zh: 是科學用語，新領域通常粗糙、描述性，

cues.en: of errors and setbacks, and it takes a long time for a field to become mature and established, for
cues.zh: 充滿錯誤、挫折，要很久才能成熟、確立，

cues.en: the foundations to be secure, for meaningful theories to be developed, and so on.
cues.zh: 基礎穩固、發展有意義理論等等。

cues.en: This was true for physics in the past.
cues.zh: 物理曾如此，

cues.en: It was true for chemistry and biology.
cues.zh: 化學、生物也是。

cues.en: It is definitely true for neuroscience and it's true for mechanistic interpretability.
cues.zh: 神經科學如此，機制可解釋性也如此。

cues.en: So in my opinion, everything on this slide is simultaneously very frustrating but also very exciting.
cues.zh: 所以既挫折，也興奮。

cues.en: There are a lot of meaningful contributions that people can make in this field, simply because it's
cues.zh: 能做很多有意義貢獻，因為

cues.en: so new and there's so much that is unknown and not yet established.
cues.zh: 很新，很多未知、未確立。

cues.en: So what do you need to know?
cues.zh: 那需要知道什麼？

cues.en: If you want to do mech interp research, or at least learn about the foundations?
cues.zh: 若想研究，至少學基礎，

cues.en: Obviously you need to have a decent grasp of LLM architecture, including the concept of embeddings,
cues.zh: 顯然要掌握 LLM 架構，包括嵌入、

cues.en: vectors, transformers, how the attention and MLP sublayers work, and so on.
cues.zh: 向量、Transformer、注意力與 MLP 子層。

cues.en: Basically, you want to have a decent grasp of understanding how token embeddings flow from the beginning to the end of a language model.
cues.zh: 基本上，要理解詞元嵌入如何從模型開頭流到結尾。

cues.en: There's also some math and coding that you need to know to do mech interp.
cues.zh: 還需要數學、程式。

cues.en: I will do my best to explain all the math that you need, as I introduce it for each analysis method in the rest of this course.
cues.zh: 後面介紹每個分析方法時，我會盡量解釋所需數學。

cues.en: Of course, you also need to be a fairly decent python coder and also be familiar with PyTorch.
cues.zh: 當然，也要有一定 Python 能力，熟悉 PyTorch。

cues.en: And this last point that I have here is based on my own experience.
cues.zh: 最後一點來自個人經驗。

cues.en: As you may know, I was a professor of neuroscience for quite a few years.
cues.zh: 你也許知道，我當過多年神經科學教授。

cues.en: I ran a neuroscience research lab where we focused on developing and applying a lot of multivariate,
cues.zh: 帶過研究室，開發、運用多變量、

cues.en: complex data analysis techniques to neural data.
cues.zh: 複雜資料分析於神經資料。

cues.en: When I first started learning about mechanistic interpretability of AI, I was immediately struck by
cues.zh: 初學 AI 機制可解釋性時，立即驚訝，

cues.en: how similar the analyses and also the challenges and just the ways of thinking about data and running experiments are certainly not identical, but quite similar.
cues.zh: 分析、挑戰、資料思考方式、實驗方法雖不完全相同，卻非常相似。

cues.en: Certainly a lot of things to recognize between neuroscience and AI.
cues.zh: 神經科學與 AI，有許多熟悉之處。

cues.en: So having any exposure to neuroscience data, I think will give you an interesting and unique perspective on studying llms.
cues.zh: 所以接觸神經資料，我認為會提供研究 LLM 的獨特、有趣觀點。

cues.en: This here is a great paper that you can find that provides a nice overview and background on mechanistic interpretability.
cues.zh: 這篇論文提供很好的概觀與背景。

cues.en: To be clear, this is not necessary reading for this course.
cues.zh: 先說，不是必讀。

cues.en: You do not need to do any outside reading for the rest of this course unless you want to.
cues.zh: 除非想要，否則剩下課程不需要額外閱讀。

cues.en: But if you're curious to learn more, there are many, many papers, many blog posts, articles on lesswrong and other websites.
cues.zh: 但好奇，有很多論文、部落格、LessWrong 文章與其他網站。

cues.en: But I think this paper here is a pretty good academic review to begin with.
cues.zh: 我覺得這篇學術綜述很適合開始。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: I hope I didn't come across as being too negative or overly critical.
cues.zh: 希望沒有太負面、太苛刻。

cues.en: I think mechanistic interpretability is one of the most fascinating areas of development in AI in my mind.
cues.zh: 依我看，這是 AI 最迷人的發展領域之一。

cues.en: The difficulties and the challenges that I described in this video are not fatal flaws, but instead
cues.zh: 那些困難、挑戰不是致命缺陷，

cues.en: are opportunities to be involved in developing a brand new field of scientific inquiry, one that has
cues.zh: 而是參與全新科學領域的機會，

cues.en: implications and applications for contributing to the safe and beneficial use of AI.
cues.zh: 有助 AI 的安全、有益使用。
